jobs.description:
Position Description

Seattle City Light, a department of the City of Seattle, is one of the nation’s largest municipally owned utilities in terms of the number of customers served. Over the years we have worked very hard to keep Seattle's electricity affordable, reliable, and environmentally sound. Today, City Light is a recognized national leader in energy efficiency and environmental stewardship.

This position serves as Seattle City Light's primary technical resource for all-hazards environmental risk analysis and program documentation, supporting the identification, assessment, and mitigation of climate-driven risks to the utility's infrastructure and operations.

Under limited supervision, this position exercises independent professional judgment across a wide range of environmental and specialized scientific fields, including forestry, wildfire behavior, extreme wind events, and flooding. This position independently determines the scope of work, budget, schedule, and compliance requirements for environmental studies and consulting contracts, and is responsible for interpreting and applying environmental and wildfire-related regulations to utility operations. This includes designing and overseeing environmental risk studies from an operational, all-hazards perspective, and leading the update of related policies, programs, standard operating procedures, and guidelines.

The role sits within the Emergency Management team and works across Operations, Engineering, Asset Management, Vegetation Management, and external partners to ensure the utility has the data, analysis, and program documentation it needs to make informed risk reduction investments. This position will report to the Emergency Management Manager.

Job Responsibilities

All-Hazards Risk Analysis and Mapping

Leads efforts related to all-hazards environmental risk mapping, including scoping, vendor management, data coordination, and delivery of risk analysis products that inform capital investment and mitigation priorities.
Commission and oversee risk studies and assessments conducted by external consultants, including wildfire risk mapping, infrastructure vulnerability analysis, and climate-driven hazard modeling.
Synthesize data from multiple sources, including LiDAR, GIS, outage history, vegetation treatment records, terrain, and weather data, into risk products that are actionable for engineers, operations staff, and executives.
Evaluate emerging environmental risks, including wildfire, high wind events, flooding, and landslides, in the context of Seattle City Light's transmission and distribution infrastructure.

Program Documentation and Compliance

Develop and maintain technical documentation, progress reports, and program records for Seattle City Light's hazard mitigation programs, including the Wildfire Risk Reduction Strategy and any successor all-hazards frameworks.
Support compliance with state and federal regulatory requirements governing utility wildfire and hazard mitigation planning, including RCW 19.29A.170 and RCW 76.04.185.
Prepare briefing materials, regulatory submittals, and City Council-facing reports that communicate program status, risk posture, and mitigation progress to a range of technical and non-technical audiences.
Develop and maintain data tracking templates, dashboards, and reporting tools that support annual progress reporting and multi-year program updates.

Capital and Technology Project Support

Review Seattle City Light's capital program portfolio and technology projects through an all-hazards environmental risk lens, identifying gaps in risk reduction coverage and opportunities to integrate mitigation measures into planned work.
Provide technical input on project scoping, prioritization, and sequencing to ensure that risk reduction objectives are reflected in capital planning decisions.
Support integration of environmental risk considerations into asset management practices and long-range infrastructure planning.
Identify and pursue federal and state grant opportunities that support all-hazards risk reduction.
Maintain awareness of the evolving federal funding landscape related to utility resilience, climate adaptation, and wildfire mitigation.

Cross-Functional Coordination and Communication

Represent all-hazards risk reduction program requirements on cross-functional teams and in coordination with Operations, Engineering, Asset Management, Environmental, and Emergency Management.
Provide technical recommendations on vegetation management priorities based on environmental risk analysis and infrastructure vulnerability data.
Coordinate data sharing and project inputs with internal teams and external partners, including vendors, consultants, state agencies, and tribal partners.
Prepare and present technical findings, risk analyses, and program updates to leadership, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Working Conditions

This position is based at Seattle City Light's South Service Center and may require periodic field visits to transmission corridors, substations, and right-of-way areas. Some travel within Washington State may be required for agency meetings, field assessments, or regulatory engagements. This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain authorization for unsupervised access to critical cyber assets, critical bulk electric assets, and electric generating facilities, including successful completion of a background check.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in natural or physical sciences, environmental sciences, planning (with emphasis on environmental issues), public administration/policy (with emphasis on natural resources), or related field and a minimum of five years experience in environmental research, environmental law, impact analysis, environmental compliance, toxic substance management, or a related field (Other combinations of education, training and experience will be evaluated on an individual basis for comparability).

Work Environment/Physical Demands

Work may be performed in the field including remote wilderness locations, on rivers and reservoirs, hazardous waste sites, household hazardous waste collection facilities and electrical facilities, and/or in a normal City office/work environment.
May require rotating on-call duty for spill response and other emergencies.
Occasional exposure to hazardous wastes, chemicals, and other conditions requiring safety precautions.

License, Certification And Other Requirements

Current State of Washington driver's license or evidence of equivalent mobility.
Hazardous materials/toxics work may require specialized health & safety training and certification.

Desired Qualifications -
You will be successful if you have the following experience, skills, and abilities:

Experience in electric utility operations, transmission and distribution infrastructure, or utility wildfire mitigation.
Experience supporting regulatory review processes, legislative reporting, or public accountability documentation.
Familiarity with FEMA's Hazard Mitigation Planning framework, the National Response Framework, or the Incident Command System.
Experience with wildfire risk modeling platforms or similar all-hazards risk assessment tools.
Graduate degree in a relevant field.
Experience independently scoping, budgeting, and managing consultant or vendor contracts for environmental or technical studies
Experience preparing technical documentation, compliance reports, or regulatory submittals for executive or public-facing audiences

Emergency Response Commitment

Seattle City Light is committed to reliable service during emergencies. Through our Emergency Response Program, each employee is assigned a role—usually aligned with their regular duties—to support emergency operations. Your participation is required and vital to helping the utility stay prepared and serve our community when it matters most.

Barr is seeking a field technician with a reality capture and survey focus to join our Minneapolis, Minnesota, office. In this hybrid role, you will use traditional survey equipment alongside reality capture technologies, including 3D scanning and drones.

The ideal candidate for this position is a clear and confident communicator who thrives in collaborative and independent work environments. They are adaptable, organized, proactive, eager to learn, and comfortable asking thoughtful questions. They bring a high level of attention to detail and take ownership of assigned tasks in dynamic field and office conditions. They demonstrate reliability, safety awareness, and a growth mindset as they build their technical skills and professional judgment.

Field duties: traditional surveying; 3D scanning; drone surveying; bathymetric surveying; sampling equipment preparation and monitoring.
Office duties: field mission planning; processing, reviewing, and interpreting field data; assisting with report preparation; point cloud registration and processing; preparing base maps and data sets using AutoCAD and other reality capture software.

Hybrid: a hybrid work arrangement may be considered for this position. This refers to splitting time between a Barr office, field sites, and a home office. This position can be based out of Barr’s Minneapolis, Minnesota, office.

Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship by Barr, now or in the future.

Experience working in the field or on a construction site.

Familiarity with drone capture workflows (Pix4D and other LiDAR/Photogrammetry applications).

jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

The Opportunity

RETTEW is seeking an experienced Wetland & Environmental Scientist II
to join our Natural Sciences team and take an active field-lead role supporting wetland and aquatic-resource investigations throughout Pennsylvania, Ohio, and West Virginia.

This opportunity is designed for an environmental professional who can independently conduct wetland delineations, make defensible field determinations, and lead wetland delineation fieldwork
.

You'll combine hands-on field science with technical documentation while working alongside environmental professionals, Project Managers, Engineers, and other technical specialists on multidisciplinary projects.

If you've developed strong wetland delineation expertise and are ready to take greater ownership of field assignments while expanding your natural-resources experience, this is an opportunity to do both.

What You'll Do

As a Wetland & Environmental Scientist II, you will:

Independently conduct and serve as field lead for wetland and stream delineations.
Apply the 1987 U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Wetland Delineation Manual and applicable regional supplements to field determinations.
Identify and document hydrophytic vegetation, hydric soils, and wetland hydrology indicators.
Establish and document wetland determination data points.
Identify and flag wetland boundaries in the field.
Identify and characterize streams and other aquatic resources.
Collect and document accurate environmental field data using GPS/GNSS and related field technology.
Complete wetland determination forms, field notes, photographic documentation, and other required field records.
Independently prepare clear, defensible wetland delineation reports and supporting technical documentation.
Prepare or support wetland and aquatic-resource mapping and project exhibits.
Coordinate field assignments and communicate project needs, findings, and potential issues to Project Managers and technical teams.
Collaborate with Engineers, Environmental Scientists, Surveyors, and other disciplines supporting project delivery.
Maintain accurate project records and support QA/QC of environmental documentation.
Support additional natural-resource investigations based on project needs and experience.
Assist with environmental permitting and regulatory coordination when applicable.

Required

What We're Looking For

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Botany, or a related natural-sciences discipline.
Demonstrated professional experience independently conducting wetland delineations and serving as a wetland delineation field lead.
Professional experience applying the 1987 U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Wetland Delineation Manual.
Professional experience applying the Eastern Mountains and Piedmont Regional Supplement.
Demonstrated ability to identify and document vegetation, hydric soils, and wetland hydrology indicators.
Experience establishing and documenting wetland determination data points.
Experience identifying and flagging wetland boundaries.
Experience identifying streams and other aquatic resources.
Experience collecting environmental field data using GPS/GNSS or comparable field technology.
Experience completing wetland delineation field forms and maintaining accurate field documentation.
Demonstrated ability to independently prepare wetland delineation reports and technical documentation.
Strong technical writing, communication, organization, and documentation skills.
Ability to work safely outdoors in rugged or uneven terrain and varying weather conditions.
Ability and willingness to travel regionally for field assignments, including periodic overnight travel.
Valid driver's license and ability to meet applicable requirements for project-related driving.

Additional Experience We Value

Experience applying the Northcentral and Northeast Regional Supplement.
Experience applying the Midwest Regional Supplement.
Clean Water Act Section 404 and/or Section 401 permitting experience.
Other wetland or aquatic-resource permitting experience.
Experience coordinating with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers or state environmental agencies.
Threatened and endangered species field-survey experience.
Experience with GIS or other environmental field-data and mapping technology.
Experience supporting multidisciplinary engineering, energy, transportation, land development, or infrastructure projects.

Build Your Natural Resources Expertise

At RETTEW, you'll have the opportunity to build on your wetland expertise while expanding your exposure to other areas of natural-resources consulting.

You can:

Take ownership of wetland delineation field assignments and serve as a trusted field resource.
Work across varied landscapes and project environments in Pennsylvania, Ohio, and West Virginia.
Strengthen your technical expertise in wetland and aquatic-resource assessment.
Gain additional exposure to environmental permitting and regulatory coordination.
Work alongside experienced Natural Sciences professionals and multidisciplinary project teams.
Expand into threatened and endangered species work and other natural-resource specialties based on project needs and interests.
Take on increasing responsibility for technical deliverables, project coordination, QA/QC, and client interaction as your career develops.
Build ownership in RETTEW through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP).

Work Environment

Workplace Designation:
Hybrid

Locations:
Pittsburgh, PA; Morgantown, WV; or Akron-Canton, OH

This is a field-intensive environmental position
that combines field assignments with office-based technical work and remote-work flexibility.

Field assignments may require walking significant distances over rugged, uneven, wet, or vegetated terrain; working outdoors in varying weather conditions; carrying field equipment; and traveling to project sites throughout the region.

Periodic overnight travel is an essential component of the position.

Safety & Compliance Requirements

This position is designated as safety-sensitive. The selected candidate must successfully complete applicable pre-employment screenings as a condition of employment.

The role includes field-based work and may involve operation of company-owned or personal vehicles for business purposes. Employees must comply with RETTEW safety policies, client-specific requirements, and applicable environmental and workplace-safety standards throughout employment.

About RETTEW

RETTEW is a 100% employee-owned engineering and consulting firm helping clients solve complex environmental and infrastructure challenges.

Our Natural Sciences professionals work alongside Engineers, Scientists, Surveyors, Project Managers, and other technical specialists to help clients understand environmental conditions, navigate regulatory requirements, and develop responsible solutions.

Our culture is grounded in our core values — Act Like an Owner, Value Relationships, and Exemplify Excellence
— and gives employees the opportunity to contribute directly to the quality and success of our work while sharing in RETTEW's long-term success through our Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP).

What We Offer

Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) — every eligible employee has the opportunity to share in RETTEW's long-term success.
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits.
Retirement savings options.
Paid time off and paid holidays.
Hybrid work environment balanced with meaningful field experience.
Professional development and opportunities to expand your technical expertise.
Exposure to multidisciplinary projects, clients, and natural-resource challenges.
Opportunities for continued technical, project, and career growth.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Position summary

The Solutions Engineer designs the operation.

When a customer needs receiving, storage, picking and shipping to work as one operation rather than as separate pieces of equipment, the Solutions Engineer analyzes their data, maps the process, designs the material flow across every functional area, and produces the concept everything downstream is built from.

The work is industrial engineering applied to a commercial pursuit: order profiles, rates, capacity, labor, and the tradeoffs between them, worked out with the customer and defensible in front of them. The Solutions Engineer hands the Application Engineer a high-level layout with the flow and the rates behind it, and the Application Engineer makes it real.

Staffing test: are we designing the operation, or equipping one that is already defined? A Solutions Engineer engages on greenfield facilities, material flow across multiple functional areas, reconfiguration or process redesign, and any pursuit with customer operational data to analyze. Replacements, expansions, defined-scope RFP responses and repeat scope run without one, and that is the normal case.

Character Qualifications

Innovation – We create a culture of relentless improvement of solutions and processes to make every day better.

Integrity – We are open, honest, and committed to giving the straight story every time.

Service – We serve our clients, families, communities, and most importantly our people who are empowered and safe in making decisions and taking actions that dare to make us better.

Ownership – We take full, personal, individual responsibility for our actions and our work.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Intake & qualification

Give the technical feasibility read on bid/no-bid. The commercial decision sits above this department.

Solution development

Analyze the customer’s data directly: order profiles, SKU velocity and slotting, volume and seasonality, labor and rate modeling. Establish the rate and capacity basis the solution is sized from.
Map the process across every functional area in scope and design the material flow that ties them into one operation: routes, buffers, decision points and interfaces.
Produce the block-level layout by functional area and select the technology class for each.
Select the third-party partners in the solution where our own product is not the answer. Commodity scope stays generic and goes to execution.
Evaluate technology feasibility and weigh the tradeoffs between options: cost, throughput, flexibility, footprint and lifecycle.

Customer & supply

Work in front of the customer alongside Sales as the technical voice on the solution.
Serve as the primary technical liaison to the customer through the pursuit, presenting and defending the concept and the tradeoffs behind it.

Execution & turnover

Hand execution a package they can build from: the reasoning and assumptions, not only the drawings.
Support the Project Manager through the early phases of execution.

Contributes to

○Reviewing the RFP, contract and statement of work for risk

○Protecting the project budget and gross margin

○Applying Fives equipment and configurations to the requirement

○Layout drawings

○Electrical and controls architecture

○The mechanical estimate

○CRD authorship

○Technical writing, description of operation and scope

○Specification compliance and acceptance criteria

○Bid strategy

○Risk assessment

○Vendor and subcontractor evaluation

○The technical basis for acceptance criteria and test procedures

○The standardization program and product classification

Qualifications

Education and experience

Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering preferred. Engineering or an equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
8 to 12 years designing automated material handling or distribution operations.
Required: ownership of facility-level or operation-level concepts spanning multiple functional areas.
Required: hands-on analysis of customer operational data, including order profiles, velocity, volumes and seasonality, and the rate and capacity modeling built on it.
Required: direct customer-facing technical experience during a sales pursuit.
Preferred, not required: material handling, distribution, parcel or baggage experience, and familiarity with AS/RS, goods-to-person, robotics and sortation technologies. Candidates from adjacent automation industries are expressly welcome.
Familiarity with discrete-event simulation, sufficient to commission and interpret it. Building the models is not required.
Excel to a high standard. SQL, Power BI or equivalent an advantage. Block-level layout in SketchUp or AutoCAD.

Skills

Language. Reads and interprets customer specifications, operational data, contracts and statements of work. Presents and defends concepts to customers and to senior management. Mathematical. Throughput, capacity and queuing analysis. Applied statistics on operational data. Geometry and trigonometry applied to facility layout. Reasoning. Defines problems, collects data, establishes facts, and draws valid conclusions from incomplete information, stating the assumptions used to get there.

Travel

Travel to customer sites, vendor plants and job sites, typically 25% to 40%. Occasional international travel for site visits or training.

Progression

The Solutions Engineer role has four levels: Junior Solutions Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Senior Solutions Engineer and Principal Solutions Engineer. Senior comes from consistently sound operation design and passing the discipline’s method review, and carries sign-off on others’ concepts along with coaching. Principal holds cross-discipline technical authority. None of these levels manages people. Line management is a separate route, through Supervisor, Manager and Director of Solutions, open by choice rather than by seniority.

Job Description Summary

Serves as the organization's subject matter expert in workforce analytics and human capital data, transforming workforce, operational, financial, economic, and organizational data into strategic insights that support executive decision-making.

Partners with HR leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to develop analytics that inform recruiting, retention, compensation, workforce planning, succession planning, employee demographics, organizational effectiveness, facilities management, space utilization, and other strategic initiatives.

Designs, develops, and maintains workforce analytics solutions, including dashboards, reporting platforms, data models, and automated reporting processes. Ensures data quality through governance, validation, and continuous improvement practices while applying advanced statistical analysis, forecasting, visualization, and predictive modeling techniques.

Leads analytics projects that expand organizational reporting capabilities and improve data-driven decision-making. Produces recurring and ad hoc reports, dashboards, presentations, and executive-level insights while advancing enterprise workforce analytics strategy in collaboration with HR leadership, the Director of Business Data Analytics, the Director of Facilities, and other organizational partners.

Serves as a trusted advisor by providing guidance on workforce metrics, reporting methodologies, dashboard functionality, and interpretation of analytics. Maintains appropriate confidentiality when handling sensitive employee and organizational information.

Responsibilities

Data Management & Analysis:
Develops and advances a comprehensive workforce analytics program that improves data availability, automation, and decision support. Conducts workforce analyses supporting talent management, workforce planning, recruiting, compensation, retention, succession planning, diversity metrics, organizational effectiveness, facilities management, and space utilization. Identifies trends, risks, and opportunities, develops actionable recommendations, and partners with leadership to establish workforce metrics, KPIs, and reporting priorities.

Data Assets & Data Integrity:

Collaborates with HR, Finance, IT, and other departments, maintaining strong cross-functional relationships to facilitate consensus and ensure alignment and consistency of workforce data. Ensures the accuracy, completeness, reliability and relevance of data sets and data models.

Dashboard Development and Management:
Designs, develops, tests, deploys, and maintains dashboards, data visualizations, and business intelligence solutions that effectively communicate workforce insights to technical and non-technical audiences. Manages dashboard releases, data pipelines, system testing, usability improvements, and performance optimization. Reporting:
Leads recurring and ad hoc workforce reporting (e.g., turnover, demographics, recruiting, succession planning) that provides leadership with timely, accurate, and actionable information. Works closely with leadership and staff to identify analytical requirements. Serves as a resource to management, responding to questions, providing guidance on best practices and approaches to modeling and analyzing data. Leads analytics initiatives from planning through implementation, including deployment of new solutions, enhancement of existing capabilities, and continuous process improvement. Builds organizational capability by mentoring colleagues, developing training resources, promoting adoption of analytics tools, and improving data literacy across HR and the broader organization.

Maintains strict confidence and exercises care when handling secure, privileged, sensitive, or confidential information and matters to prevent disclosure to others. Accesses confidential information for work-related reasons only, following the policies and procedures of the organization. Position Description

Seattle City Light, a department of the City of Seattle, is one of the nation’s largest municipally owned utilities in terms of the number of customers served. Over the years we have worked very hard to keep Seattle's electricity affordable, reliable, and environmentally sound. Today, City Light is a recognized national leader in energy efficiency and environmental stewardship.

This position serves as Seattle City Light's primary technical resource for all-hazards environmental risk analysis and program documentation, supporting the identification, assessment, and mitigation of climate-driven risks to the utility's infrastructure and operations.

Under limited supervision, this position exercises independent professional judgment across a wide range of environmental and specialized scientific fields, including forestry, wildfire behavior, extreme wind events, and flooding. This position independently determines the scope of work, budget, schedule, and compliance requirements for environmental studies and consulting contracts, and is responsible for interpreting and applying environmental and wildfire-related regulations to utility operations. This includes designing and overseeing environmental risk studies from an operational, all-hazards perspective, and leading the update of related policies, programs, standard operating procedures, and guidelines.

The role sits within the Emergency Management team and works across Operations, Engineering, Asset Management, Vegetation Management, and external partners to ensure the utility has the data, analysis, and program documentation it needs to make informed risk reduction investments. This position will report to the Emergency Management Manager.

Job Responsibilities

All-Hazards Risk Analysis and Mapping

Leads efforts related to all-hazards environmental risk mapping, including scoping, vendor management, data coordination, and delivery of risk analysis products that inform capital investment and mitigation priorities.
Commission and oversee risk studies and assessments conducted by external consultants, including wildfire risk mapping, infrastructure vulnerability analysis, and climate-driven hazard modeling.
Synthesize data from multiple sources, including LiDAR, GIS, outage history, vegetation treatment records, terrain, and weather data, into risk products that are actionable for engineers, operations staff, and executives.
Evaluate emerging environmental risks, including wildfire, high wind events, flooding, and landslides, in the context of Seattle City Light's transmission and distribution infrastructure.

Program Documentation and Compliance

Develop and maintain technical documentation, progress reports, and program records for Seattle City Light's hazard mitigation programs, including the Wildfire Risk Reduction Strategy and any successor all-hazards frameworks.
Support compliance with state and federal regulatory requirements governing utility wildfire and hazard mitigation planning, including RCW 19.29A.170 and RCW 76.04.185.
Prepare briefing materials, regulatory submittals, and City Council-facing reports that communicate program status, risk posture, and mitigation progress to a range of technical and non-technical audiences.
Develop and maintain data tracking templates, dashboards, and reporting tools that support annual progress reporting and multi-year program updates.

Capital and Technology Project Support

Review Seattle City Light's capital program portfolio and technology projects through an all-hazards environmental risk lens, identifying gaps in risk reduction coverage and opportunities to integrate mitigation measures into planned work.
Provide technical input on project scoping, prioritization, and sequencing to ensure that risk reduction objectives are reflected in capital planning decisions.
Support integration of environmental risk considerations into asset management practices and long-range infrastructure planning.
Identify and pursue federal and state grant opportunities that support all-hazards risk reduction.
Maintain awareness of the evolving federal funding landscape related to utility resilience, climate adaptation, and wildfire mitigation.

Cross-Functional Coordination and Communication

Represent all-hazards risk reduction program requirements on cross-functional teams and in coordination with Operations, Engineering, Asset Management, Environmental, and Emergency Management.
Provide technical recommendations on vegetation management priorities based on environmental risk analysis and infrastructure vulnerability data.
Coordinate data sharing and project inputs with internal teams and external partners, including vendors, consultants, state agencies, and tribal partners.
Prepare and present technical findings, risk analyses, and program updates to leadership, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Working Conditions

This position is based at Seattle City Light's South Service Center and may require periodic field visits to transmission corridors, substations, and right-of-way areas. Some travel within Washington State may be required for agency meetings, field assessments, or regulatory engagements. This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain authorization for unsupervised access to critical cyber assets, critical bulk electric assets, and electric generating facilities, including successful completion of a background check.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in natural or physical sciences, environmental sciences, planning (with emphasis on environmental issues), public administration/policy (with emphasis on natural resources), or related field and a minimum of five years experience in environmental research, environmental law, impact analysis, environmental compliance, toxic substance management, or a related field (Other combinations of education, training and experience will be evaluated on an individual basis for comparability).

Work Environment/Physical Demands

Work may be performed in the field including remote wilderness locations, on rivers and reservoirs, hazardous waste sites, household hazardous waste collection facilities and electrical facilities, and/or in a normal City office/work environment.
May require rotating on-call duty for spill response and other emergencies.
Occasional exposure to hazardous wastes, chemicals, and other conditions requiring safety precautions.

License, Certification And Other Requirements

Current State of Washington driver's license or evidence of equivalent mobility.
Hazardous materials/toxics work may require specialized health & safety training and certification.

Desired Qualifications -
You will be successful if you have the following experience, skills, and abilities:

Experience in electric utility operations, transmission and distribution infrastructure, or utility wildfire mitigation.
Experience supporting regulatory review processes, legislative reporting, or public accountability documentation.
Familiarity with FEMA's Hazard Mitigation Planning framework, the National Response Framework, or the Incident Command System.
Experience with wildfire risk modeling platforms or similar all-hazards risk assessment tools.
Graduate degree in a relevant field.
Experience independently scoping, budgeting, and managing consultant or vendor contracts for environmental or technical studies

Position summary

The Solutions Engineer designs the operation.

When a customer needs receiving, storage, picking and shipping to work as one operation rather than as separate pieces of equipment, the Solutions Engineer analyzes their data, maps the process, designs the material flow across every functional area, and produces the concept everything downstream is built from.

The work is industrial engineering applied to a commercial pursuit: order profiles, rates, capacity, labor, and the tradeoffs between them, worked out with the customer and defensible in front of them. The Solutions Engineer hands the Application Engineer a high-level layout with the flow and the rates behind it, and the Application Engineer makes it real.

Staffing test: are we designing the operation, or equipping one that is already defined? A Solutions Engineer engages on greenfield facilities, material flow across multiple functional areas, reconfiguration or process redesign, and any pursuit with customer operational data to analyze. Replacements, expansions, defined-scope RFP responses and repeat scope run without one, and that is the normal case.
